title: ‘Who would apply medicine to child’s blisters?’ Delhi techie killed over chore; wife, in-laws held
content: A software engineer died after an argument over household chores escalated. His wife and her brothers allegedly attacked and strangled him at his home. The victim's family members were also assaulted during the violent altercation. Police have arrested four individuals in connection with the software engineer's death. Investigations are ongoing into the matrimonial disputes which preceded the incident.

title: Christ University files complaint after ABVP gherao, vandalism, assault on guards
content: Christ University filed a complaint against ABVP activists for trespassing and vandalism.  Protesters blocked the campus entrance demanding promotion for 13 law students.  The university cited damage to property and disruption of student movement.  Police are investigating the allegations and have increased security presence.  An examination committee will review the students' demands next week.

title: 'Masters in our own home': Canada PM Carney explains why talks with US were suspended
content: Canada has halted trade negotiations with the United States due to perceived inequities in demands, leading to the US imposing hefty tariffs on Canadian exports. In response, Canada has unveiled countermeasures to address these tariffs. Prime Minister Carney criticized the US for its unreasonable requests while providing insufficient concessions. This escalation raises alarms about the future of economic collaboration between the two nations.

title: Microsoft has a 6-word answer for students wondering if coding is still worth it
content: Microsoft Learn has told students on X that learning to code is worth it "now more than ever", even as AI writes a growing share of software. Satya Nadella says AI already produces up to 30% of Microsoft's code, while Google puts its figure at 75%. The skill has not died, it has shifted from writing syntax to reviewing, debugging and directing AI-generated code.

title: Saransh Jain makes India debut at 33: Who is the allrounder taking on Sri Lanka?
content: Saransh Jain celebrated a significant breakthrough on Sunday by making his Test debut for India at 33, facing off against Sri Lanka. With more than a decade's worth of domestic experiences behind him, Jain's impressive red-ball track record led to this noteworthy selection, making him the first Indian player to debut after turning 33 since 1998.

title: Ganpati idol falls during procession in Mumbai; 2 dead, 5 injured
content: Two individuals died and five others sustained injuries when a large Ganpati idol collapsed during its procession. The idol fell due to an apparent welding issue with its supporting frame, police officials stated. The incident occurred late Saturday night as the procession neared its destination in Bhuleshwar. The deceased included the Ganpati mandal president, Sanket Nevshe. Investigations into the exact circumstances of the accident are currently underway by authorities.

title: Meta sued by former manager who claims he was fired over immigration letter
content: A former Meta manager filed a lawsuit alleging wrongful termination after objecting to an immigration letter. James Tillinghast claimed the letter overstated an employee's contributions and responsibilities. He also alleged Meta provided preferential immigration support to certain Chinese national employees. Tillinghast believes his dismissal was retaliation for raising these concerns. The lawsuit names Meta Platforms and a manager as defendants.

title: Gujarat store owner shot dead in US in front of 19-year-old daughter
content: A 56-year-old Gujarati man was fatally shot during a liquor store robbery. The gunman demanded cash and then fired multiple shots inside the premises. His 19-year-old daughter stood beside him but remained unharmed during the incident. Another employee suffered a fractured wrist after falling during the shooting. Police are actively searching for the unidentified suspect and his vehicle.

title: Gurugram founder turns salon hair waste into mats that clean polluted water
content: Salons' discarded human hair has found a new life as pollution-absorbing mats. These innovative mats intercept contaminants in drains, preventing them from entering larger water bodies. Utilizing the natural oil-absorbing properties of keratin in hair, the HydroHair Barrier System has shown promise in pilot tests, leading to reductions in key pollution indicators.

title: Medical debt relief model: MacKenzie Scott’s gifts erase $40 billion; $10 cancels $1,000
content: MacKenzie Scott pioneered large-scale medical debt relief through significant donations. Her gifts enabled the abolition of over forty billion dollars in medical debt. This initiative has provided relief to millions of families across all fifty states. Scott's model has also inspired other billionaires to contribute to debt eradication efforts. While philanthropic efforts offer immediate relief, systemic reforms are needed for lasting change.

title: Portugal get their revenge on Spain — this time in cricket — after WC heartbreak
content: Portugal secured a cricket victory over Spain, avenging their football World Cup defeat.  The Portuguese team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C.  This triumph keeps Portugal's dream of reaching the 2028 T20 World Cup alive.  Spain's chase faltered after Portugal posted a competitive total of 160 runs.  Portugal's bowlers delivered a strong performance to secure the 57-run win.

title: ‘Could result in injury or death’: Thanedar urges halting ICE’s electric shock glove plan
content: Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar and colleagues oppose ICE's electric shock glove plan.  They warn of potential misuse and severe injury or death from these devices.  Lawmakers cite ICE's past record and insufficient training for officers.  The proposed procurement involves millions of dollars for thousands of gloves.  They implore the Homeland Security Secretary to immediately stop this purchase.

title: Yash sends a strong message on ‘North-South’ comparison at ‘Toxic’ pre-release event
content: During a recent event, actor Yash expressed his gratitude towards the Telugu audience, emphasizing the expanding influence of cinema. He highlighted that talent and diligence transcend language barriers, fostering unity among viewers. Yash inspired students to aim high and accept their failures, encouraging the youth to rise above regional differences in the film industry. His much-anticipated project, 'Toxic', is scheduled for release on August 26.

title: Batwara 1947: Sunny Deol film crosses Rs 51cr worldwide amid clash with Awarapan 2
content: In its ninth day of release, Batwara 1947 managed to earn Rs 1.15 crore, bringing its total net collection in India to Rs 35.50 crore. Additionally, the film's overseas earnings accounted for Rs 9.00 crore, resulting in a global gross of Rs 51.12 crore. Unfortunately, the film directed by Rajkumar Santoshi did not achieve the expected success at the box office.

title: No work, no study, no training: 8.7 crore Indian youth caught in a career gap
content: With over eight crore Indian youth facing unemployment, a lack of vital skills hampers their job prospects. Financial barriers restrict many students from accessing crucial paid training programs, while graduates frequently settle for low-paying positions to assist their families financially. There is a stark career mismatch, as only a fraction of graduates find appropriate roles, making subsidized training and earn-as-you-learn opportunities essential for career advancement.

title: From tape-ball to 'dream of Harman’s wicket', Maryam follows her father’s dream
content: Hong Kong's vice-captain Maryam Bibi is gearing up for a pivotal challenge as she faces India. Her cricketing journey began with tape-ball games and has evolved into representing her nation on a larger stage. With aspirations to honor her father's dream, Bibi sees the match not only as a competitive opportunity but also as a source of inspiration for aspiring young female cricketers.

title: Govinda issues notice against defamatory content amid spat with wife Sunita Ahuja
content: Govinda, the celebrated actor, has taken a stand against false and defamatory content in a public notice. This alert focuses specifically on AI-generated images and misleading reports about his family. Emphasizing that no one has permission to manipulate his identity, he has threatened civil and criminal proceedings against those who violate these stipulations, aiming to combat the rampant spread of misinformation and rumors online.

title: Shoriful Islam makes history with record seven-wicket haul against Australia
content: Shoriful Islam achieved a historic seven-wicket haul against Australia in the second Test. His exceptional bowling figures of 7/48 marked a significant achievement for Bangladesh cricket. Australia secured a first-innings lead of 146 runs after being bowled out for 210. Earlier, Mitchell Starc's six-wicket haul had restricted Bangladesh to just 64 runs. Bangladesh face a challenging task to avoid defeat.

title: U'khand disaster aid for damaged houses: Check eligibility, benefits & more
content: Uttarakhand disaster authority is stepping up to provide financial assistance for homes affected by recent calamities. The amount of aid is determined by the severity of the damage and the type of dwelling—pucca or kutcha houses receive different levels of support. Even huts and cattle sheds can qualify for aid, but relief funds will only be distributed after thorough verification by the officials.

title: Amid tensions with Hegseth, US Army secy Dan Driscoll to step down by year-end
content: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is reportedly planning to leave his position by late 2026.  This departure follows months of reported tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.  Driscoll's exit could leave the Army without a Senate-confirmed leader.  The Army also currently lacks a Senate-confirmed chief of staff.  These developments signal significant changes at the Pentagon's senior levels.

title: Ronaldo becomes first player in the Football history to achieve unprecedented feat
content: Cristiano Ronaldo has reached an incredible milestone in football by scoring in twenty-five consecutive league seasons. This unprecedented achievement highlights his enduring talent, having maintained an unbroken scoring streak that dates back to the 2002-03 season. With a career total of nine hundred seventy-seven goals, he remains focused on reaching the remarkable one thousand goal mark in his illustrious career.

title: 5.9 earthquake rattles Japan: 23 injured, trains disrupted; no tsunami threat
content: In the early hours of Sunday, eastern Japan experienced a moderate earthquake, with injuries reported for over twenty individuals, primarily minor. The strong tremors caused significant disruptions in transportation services, including train delays across the region. A water pipe burst was noted in Tokyo, alongside power outages affecting numerous homes. Fortunately, no tsunami threat emerged, and nuclear facilities remained secure.

title: Awarapan 2 Day 9: Emraan Hashmi film tops Rs 180cr worldwide despite Batwara 1947 clash
content: Awarapan 2 has taken the box office by storm, crossing the landmark of one hundred crore rupees. After a remarkable surge in earnings on its ninth day, the film's total net collection in India now stands at one hundred twenty-seven point five zero crore. Additionally, overseas collections have played a significant role in boosting its overall global revenue. This action-packed sequel follows the footsteps of the beloved 2007 movie Awarapan.

title: Kuldeep or Saransh? The subplot thickens as Colombo braces for a different script
content: Kuldeep Yadav's absence from India's final training sessions has intensified the selection intrigue ahead of the Colombo Test, with Saransh Jain's strong showing in the nets and Sri Lanka's left-hand-heavy batting line-up adding weight to the off-spinner's case. The second Test between India and Sri Lanka will start from Sunday at the Sinhalese Sports Club ground in Colombo.

title: Ex-IAF vice-chief says 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s
content: A retired Air Marshal criticizes Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's delays in Tejas fighter jet deliveries. He questions why promised capabilities remain unavailable due to unfulfilled promises. Advanced Tejas Mk2 may not be operationally relevant when China deploys fifth-generation fighters. India should partner with European consortiums for sixth-generation combat aircraft development. Faster development of indigenous fifth and sixth-generation fighters is strongly desired.

title: Government cannot force private landowners to execute sale deeds for acquisition of land: Allahabad High Court
content: With this, the court directed the authorities not to harass the petitioners or forcibly obtain their consent for executing sale deeds. It also made it clear that voluntary sale and compulsory acquisition are two distinct legal processes.

title: Chicken chain co-founder restores 3,000-acre Texas ranch, revives lost springs
content: the land was washed away, native plants were gone, and the natural springs had completely dried up . the property was essentially a desolate expanse that most ranchers considered beyond saving . he launched an ambitious project to bring the land back to life with decades of careful work and ecological planning .

title: Reddy denied US visit, Gujarat CM cleared: Overseas Congress alleges ‘double standard’

title: Why Assam wants to shrink Kaziranga National Park's eco-sensitive zone
content: If people living around Kaziranga are displaced, who will protect Kaziranga?
